stories.headline: Musk Drops Fraud Claims Against OpenAI, Narrowing $134B Trial to Two Key Claims

key_facts.fact: US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers dismissed Musk's fraud and constructive fraud claims at his own request on April 24, leaving only two of the original 26 claims: unjust enrichment and breach of charitable trust.
key_facts.excerpt: On April 24th, US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers agreed to dismiss Musk's fraud and constructive fraud claims in a bid to streamline the case. This would leave just two claims to proceed to trial of the 26 originally included in his November 2024 complaint.

key_facts.fact: Jury selection is scheduled for Monday April 27 at federal court in Oakland, California, with opening arguments to follow on Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Jury selection is scheduled to begin Monday, with opening arguments to follow on Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Musk is seeking up to $134 billion in damages from OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming OpenAI betrayed its founding nonprofit mission. He said proceeds would go to OpenAI's charitable arm if he wins.
key_facts.excerpt: He is seeking damages of up to $134 billion, which he said should be directed to OpenAI's charitable arm if he succeeds.

key_facts.fact: Musk alleges OpenAI deviated from its founding nonprofit mission after securing billions from Microsoft and transitioning to a for-profit structure. He contributed $38 million in seed funding in 2015.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk argues that OpenAI was founded as a nonprofit but later turned into a for-profit company with backing from Microsoft. He says he contributed $38 million in seed funding in 2015.

key_facts.fact: Musk strategically dropped fraud claims to focus jurors on whether OpenAI benefits humanity rather than serving as a 'wealth machine,' avoiding complex evidentiary hurdles around intent.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Musk, this would allow jurors to focus on his goal of ensuring that OpenAI benefits humanity rather than serving as a 'wealth machine.'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI, Altman, Brockman, and Microsoft have denied the allegations, calling the lawsuit 'part of Musk's ongoing pattern of harassment' and accusing him of trying to benefit his own AI company, xAI.
key_facts.excerpt: The company and its leaders have all denied wrongdoing, with OpenAI claiming that the lawsuit is 'part of [Musk's] ongoing pattern of harassment.' The company also said that Musk is trying to slow them down and benefit his own business, xAI.

stories.headline: Epoch AI: Google Controls ~25% of Global AI Compute With 3.8M TPUs, Leading All Hyperscalers

key_facts.fact: Google is the largest single owner of AI compute, holding about one quarter of global cumulative capacity as of Q4 2025, according to Epoch AI's Chip Ownership data.
key_facts.excerpt: We estimate Google is the largest single owner of AI compute, holding about one quarter of global cumulative capacity as of Q4 2025.

key_facts.fact: Google's compute comes primarily from its own custom TPU chips rather than Nvidia's GPUs, making it unique among hyperscalers. Google has approximately 3.8 million TPUs and 1.3 million GPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: Notably among hyperscalers, Google's compute comes primarily from its own custom TPU chips rather than NVIDIA's GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Five hyperscalers — Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle — collectively hold an estimated 71% of the world's cumulative AI compute, up from 63% in Q1 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle collectively hold an estimated 71% of the world's cumulative AI compute as of Q4 2025, measured in H100-equivalents of computing power. This is up from 63% in Q1 2024.

key_facts.fact: Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian told the Financial Times that demand and revenue justify the massive compute investment, arguing the company's AI chips and models can help the data centre business gain ground.
key_facts.excerpt: Thomas Kurian, Google Cloud's CEO, says its AI chips and models can help the data centre business gain ground.

stories.headline: Anthropic Reaches $1 Trillion Valuation on Secondary Markets, Surpassing OpenAI's $880B

key_facts.fact: On Forge Global, a private share marketplace, Anthropic's implied valuation has climbed to roughly $1 trillion, surpassing OpenAI which trades at $880 billion on the same platform.
key_facts.excerpt: On Forge Global, a private share marketplace, Anthropic's implied valuation has climbed to roughly $1 trillion — putting it ahead of OpenAI, which trades at $880 billion on the same platform.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's last primary funding round, led by GIC and Coatue roughly three months ago, valued the company at $380 billion — less than half of what the secondary market now implies.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's own most recent primary round — a GIC- and Coatue-led deal that closed roughly three months ago — set its valuation at $380 billion, less than half what the secondary market now implies.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate surged from $9 billion late last year to $30 billion by March 2026, driven largely by breakout adoption of Claude Code among developers.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue figures reported by Business Insider show the company's annualized run rate surging from $9 billion late last year to $30 billion by March 2026, a jump that analysts have tied largely to breakout adoption of its Claude Code tool among developers.

key_facts.fact: A shortage of available shares is fueling buyer frenzy. One shareholder offered to sell at a $1.15 trillion valuation, while a 'very well known growth fund' bid at $1.05 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: Ken Sawyer, cofounder and managing partner at Saints Capital, said one shareholder had offered to sell at a $1.15 trillion valuation. A 'very well known growth fund' offered to buy at $1.05 trillion.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has reportedly been rejecting investment offers at an $800 billion valuation in recent days, while current shareholders report being inundated with unsolicited approaches.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's last funding round valued it at $380 billion. The company has reportedly been rejecting investment offers at an $800 billion valuation in recent days.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's position on secondary markets looks markedly different: interest has been thin, with buyers unwilling to match the price from the company's last fundraise.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's position in the secondary market looks markedly different: Anderson said interest there has been thin, with buyers unwilling to match even the price set during the company's last fundraise.

stories.headline: ASML Plans to Build at Least 60 EUV Machines in 2026, Up 36% From 2025 Sales

key_facts.fact: ASML plans to make at least 60 of its standard EUV lithography machines in 2026, a 36% increase over the number it sold in 2025, as it races to meet demand for AI chip production.
key_facts.excerpt: ASML says it plans to make at least 60 of its standard EUV machines this year, 36% more than it sold in 2025, as it races to meet demand for making AI chips.

key_facts.fact: ASML is the sole supplier of EUV lithography machines needed to manufacture cutting-edge AI chips at scale, giving it a monopoly position in the supply chain.
key_facts.excerpt: ASML is the only supplier of the machines needed to make cutting edge AI chips at scale.

key_facts.fact: ASML's order backlog stood at €38.8 billion at the end of 2025, and the company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to €34–39 billion, well above prior analyst estimates.
key_facts.excerpt: ASML's order backlog already stood at €38.8 billion at the end of 2025. The company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to €34–39 billion, well above prior analyst estimates.

key_facts.fact: The production ramp at ASML's Veldhoven headquarters in the Netherlands highlights the critical bottleneck in AI chip manufacturing infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: VELDHOVEN, the Netherlands — ASML is the only supplier of the machines needed to make cutting edge AI chips at scale.

stories.headline: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab Grows to ~140 Staff, Hiring Most From Meta

key_facts.fact: LinkedIn profile analysis shows Thinking Machines Lab has hired more researchers from Meta than from any other employer, with headcount now at approximately 140.
key_facts.excerpt: LinkedIn profile review shows Thinking Machines Lab has been hiring more researchers from Meta than from any other employer; TML's headcount now stands at ~140.

key_facts.fact: Thinking Machines Lab was founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati and raised a record $2 billion seed round at a $12 billion valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines is at ~140 staff, hiring more from Meta than any other lab.

key_facts.fact: The hiring pattern is notable given Meta's own aggressive AI push, including a 'superintelligence' lab, multibillion-dollar AI infrastructure deals, and reported offers of up to $1 billion to recruit individual AI researchers.
key_facts.excerpt: Notable given Meta's Scale deal and superintelligence push — top researchers still voting with their feet on culture and mission.
